item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If we're stating our desires or lack thereof, I’m 100% down with my articles being declassed, given the declassifier has me review their final draft before posting. As stated above by Nat, spreading misleading information about ambiguous articles is not something I want to promote, especially when 99% of my SCPs and tales exist within a running series and canon that hinges on interconnectivity.

A fair amount of my articles are characterized by lots of story being communicated non-chronologically or in very few words, which SCPD seems to like, but I want to ensure that any official interpretations of my works are correct and more-or-less on-topic.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Main points are that, going from interactions with fellow authors, a lot of the times declassifications can get information completely misconstrued, sending ideas completely against author intent. In a "no canon" context like the wiki's this would ordinarily be fine, but with SCPD essentially being portrayed as the center for explanations it can be taken as the word of god — especially for an off-site fanbase with no wiki involvement nor knowledge of "there is no canon." This gets further complicated in how many declassifications try to explain parts of articles which, by author intent, are not meant to be explained at all or are meant to be open ended.

Asides from that, I don't want declassifications because of my articles specifically because A: the point about wanting to preserve intentionally mysteries, and B: if I accidentally make an article hard to understand, or mess up in a similar way which obfuscates or misconstrues meaning, I don't want to resort to using an extra resource to explain things in my steed. I'd rather it be on my onus to convey the information I intend to convey, not on a declassified's. I want to be accountable for any writing mistakes I make.

Apologies if this reads overly harsh; I wanted to get my two cents down as comprehensively as possible.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for your reply!

However, as far as I know, only SCP derivative works is not enough to apply CC BY-SA 3.0 License. You must write clearly "Title", "Author", "Source", and "License(CC BY-SA 3.0)" like bottom of this wiki's top page.

SCPD's Reddit Page seems not to be written any descriptions. On the contrary, Reddit's License prohibits re-printing. I think it is conflicting with CC BY-SA 3.0 License.

Anyway, SCPD cannot be applied CC BY-SA 3.0 License currently, and I think it cannot be applied this license.

item.title: GIANT UPDATE TIME
item.content:encoded: It's a new year, and we're coming back from hiatus! In just the past 30 days, we've posted nine declassifications and gotten 4 new contributors. You can find a lot of new content in our archives, including explanations of Captain Kirby's Proposal, two 4000 contest entries, the infamous SCP-343, and a lot more. Take a read, and of course, drop your requests in our stickied thread on the subreddit!

This isn't significant in any way because this is a hub page. But wow, thanks to the SCP community for lending their support to us.

I know it says we're on hiatus, we promise we're coming back soon

item.title: One Year.
item.content:encoded:
